standard.title: Share content and collaborate
standard.description: use the core features of common digital tools to share content, plan tasks, and collaborate, following agreed behaviours, supported by trusted adults
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use basic features of digital tools to share content and collaborate, demonstrating agreed behaviours guided by trusted adults (AC9TDI2P05). They have shared content in simple, supervised contexts. They have not yet used digital tools to plan tasks collaboratively or manage shared content across a group project.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use core features of digital tools to share content, plan tasks and collaborate with peers, following agreed behaviours and supported by trusted adults.

nodes.label: Sharing content selectively and safely
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share content with a specific, appropriate audience while keeping personal information appropriately private
nodes.minimum_width: Share content with an agreed audience (e.g. a class folder, the teacher) without revealing specific personal details
nodes.typical_width: Share content in different collaboration contexts (shared folder, class survey, group document); explain which details should be kept private when sharing with different audiences; demonstrate agreed behaviours when sharing
wider: Discuss a scenario where content shared for a legitimate purpose (e.g. sharing a holiday adventure) could inadvertently reveal personal information — identify what should be removed and why
Compare the audience reach of different sharing methods (shared folder vs link vs public post) — discuss which is appropriate for different collaboration contexts

response_modes.reason: Students often focus on whether they are allowed to share rather than what information sharing reveals. Different sharing contexts (class only, school, public) help students develop a contextual understanding of appropriate sharing rather than a binary 'allowed/not allowed' rule.

success_criteria: Shares content only with the agreed audience
Does not include specific personal details (exact dates, specific names, location) in shared content
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who have not developed contextual sharing judgement will make inappropriate disclosures in N2 and N3 collaborative tasks — knowing what to share with which audience is prerequisite to participating safely in any collaborative digital activity.

nodes.label: Using digital tools to plan tasks collaboratively
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a digital tool to plan and organise a collaborative task with peers
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute to a shared planning document or survey to help organise a group task, following agreed steps
nodes.typical_width: Use digital tools to jointly plan an event or task (e.g. a class survey for an end-of-year party, a shared schedule); contribute ideas and respond to others' contributions following agreed behaviours
wider: Plan a multi-step collaborative task using a shared digital tool — assign roles, track progress and update the plan as the task develops; discuss how digital tools make coordination easier for larger groups
Design and administer a class survey using a digital tool — analyse the results collaboratively and use them to make a group decision; discuss how planning tools support group decision-making

response_modes.reason: Collaborative planning using digital tools is a capability that develops across different tool types and task complexities. Students who only plan using one tool type often cannot transfer the practice. Building repertoire across survey tools, shared documents and scheduling tools strengthens the capability.

success_criteria: Makes at least one substantive contribution to the shared planning activity
Follows agreed behaviours when interacting with peers in the digital environment

nodes.label: Collaborating online with agreed behaviours
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in an online collaboration following agreed behaviours — taking turns, respecting others' contributions, and adding to shared content constructively
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in one collaborative online task (e.g. adding to a shared slide deck or document), following at least two agreed behaviours
nodes.typical_width: Participate in collaborative online tasks across different formats; listen to and respond to others' contributions; add content that builds on what others have contributed rather than replacing or ignoring it
wider: Collaborate on a task with students from a different class or year level using digital tools — discuss how agreed behaviours need to be explicitly established when collaborating with people you do not know well
Reflect on a collaborative experience and identify one thing that went well and one that could be improved — discuss how agreed behaviours help resolve conflicts in online collaboration

response_modes.reason: Agreed behaviours in online collaboration need to transfer across tools and audiences. Students who only practise within their own familiar class context may not understand why behaviours need to be re-established with new collaborators or in new tools.

success_criteria: Adds content to a shared digital space following agreed behaviours
Responds to others' contributions in a way that builds on rather than ignores them
